Đàn tính（越南十六弦琴）又稱 tính tẩu，屬弦鳴樂器，源自中國壯族: The đàn tính, also called tính tẩu, is a chordophone that comes from the tianqin of the Chinese Zhuang and was brought in by the Tày people of Lạng Sơn province in Vietnam. It has two to four strings in two to four courses; the strings may be silk, nylon or fishing line. The traditional form has a long neck, a wooden body and a gourd or bamboo-tube soundbox, and can be taken apart; the modern form is shorter. The player sings while playing, and in earlier times the tianpo used it in possession rituals to cure illness and avert disaster; later it also became popular entertainment.
此琴屬弦鳴樂器，來源所載材質以傳統與現代形制分述。傳統琴頸為木製，琴頭雕成鳳、印: The instrument is a chordophone, and the source describes the materials separately for the traditional and the modern form. The traditional neck is wooden, the head carved as a phoenix, a seal, the sun or the moon, and fitted with wooden tuning pegs; the soundbox is made from a gourd or a hemp-bamboo tube, the soundboard from eleven pieces of glued hemp-bamboo shell or thin paulownia board, with a pattern carved at the back end as a sound window; the bridge is of bamboo and the strings of silk. The modern neck is a half-cylinder with no decoration and a flat head, whose material the source does not state; the soundbox is of tianma bamboo or iron, and the strings are silk or nylon. Another source says fishing line can be used for the strings; the materials of the other parts are not stated.

越南十六弦琴實際出現於諒山省岱族的巫儀與吟唱場合。來源指出，它早期由巫師在降神會: The đàn tính is actually heard on the shamanic and singing occasions of the Tày people in Lạng Sơn province. The source notes that in earlier times it was played by shamans at spirit-possession ceremonies, in the belief that the instrument was driven by spirit power; later this kind of song, playing and dance became popular entertainment, still performed with singing, playing and dancing at once. It also often goes with the "then" singing style, so in listening you can attend to the passages where voice and instrument interweave and the rhythm has something of ritual and dance.
越南十六弦琴源自中國壯族的天琴，後由諒山省的岱族（Tày）傳入越南，並在壯族中的: The đàn tính comes from the tianqin of the Chinese Zhuang and was brought into Vietnam by the Tày of Lạng Sơn province, passing among the Pian people of the Zhuang and the Tày. In early times the Tianpo (woman shaman) used it to cure illness and avert disaster, and in the long feudal period it was regarded as sacred, used only by the Tianpo in the "jumping to heaven" ritual; afterwards this singing, playing and dancing with its shamanic colour became popular entertainment. In 2007 the Vietnamese Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism put forward a programme to promote it, recommending that traditional songs be transcribed, recordings made, and this music taught in local arts schools; the instrument also often accompanies "Then" singing.
越南十六弦琴音色清澈透亮，具有獨特的金屬質感與溫潤韻味。其音域寬廣，跨越三個八度: The đàn tính has a clear, transparent timbre with a particular metallic quality and a warm charm. Its range is wide, spanning three octaves: deep and full in the bass, rounded and warm in the middle, bright and crisp in the treble. The strings are plucked or played with finger technique, and the resonance is layered and rings on. Its sound has the elegance of the konghou and the inwardness of the guqin, at once the poetic quality of Eastern strings and a light, lively modern feel. Beside the desolation of the Chinese guqin the đàn tính is more cheerful; beside the harp its timbre has more of an Eastern spirit and its resonance is deeper. The whole sound keeps its national character and can also express delicate layers of feeling.
